title: flow publish refusal: the "invalid expression" header always explains template braces, even when the refusal under it is a date-text or other verdict with no braces
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZiaBg6rk7dpy1s9Me

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding from the #34660 os-dev report (PR #35358), routed by its L1 ACCEPT (7001828368, 范围外去向). Pre-existing, not caused by that PR. ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets lane and grade.

## What the user sees

Registering (publishing or booting) a record-triggered flow whose `assignment` value is `timestamp(record.borrow_date)` on a date field throws:

> Flow … has 1 invalid expression (ADR-0032 §1a). Predicates — conditions and declared bare-CEL slots … — must not wrap references in {…} template braces, and neither may a value slot …

The refusal listed under it is a date-text verdict; the expression has no braces. The author is first told about a mistake they did not make.

## Where

`packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts` (~:1047-1051 at the #35358 base): one fixed header for every failure kind. Reproduced on the built `@objectstack/service-automation` by the #34660 dev.

## Fix direction

Name the braces rule only when a listed refusal is a brace refusal (`cel-template-brace` / `template-single-brace` / dialect mismatch); otherwise a neutral count header.

Dedupe: issue search `registerFlow refusal header template braces`, `invalid expression header misleading`, `flow-registration-checks preamble` → none.
